headline: Multimodal fusion models predict cancer survival and synthetic lethality from…
label: Multimodal Biomedical Prediction Models
summary: Integrating clinical text, genomics and pathology under missing-modality and calibration constraints is becoming central to TCGA-based cancer prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is multimodal integration of heterogeneous cancer data for prediction. The locally deployable LLM framework fuses clinical text, covariates and genomics for survival prediction on TCGA and emphasizes calibrated outputs, which is the element most explicitly stressed across these items. MUST addresses survival prediction from multimodal TCGA data by using diffusion-based generation to handle missing pathology or genomics modalities, a practical constraint that real cohorts routinely impose. SynLeaF applies a dual-stage multimodal fusion framework with VAE cross-encoders to synthetic lethality prediction across pan- and single-cancer contexts, extending the fusion paradigm beyond survival endpoints. What is new relative to accuracy-driven fusion models is attention to calibration in deployable settings and to incomplete modality profiles. The three items share a fusion strategy rather than a single modeling architecture or evaluation protocol, and calibration is demonstrated explicitly only in the LLM study.
